mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over prior 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC remains negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand that drives positive corporate earnings and S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS increase, or Rank IC for interaction falls below 0.02 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), rising employment (PAYEMS) signals tight labor markets that fuel wage growth and corporate profit margins, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM, or Rank IC is negative over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the prior 3 months indicates improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.04 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 for two consecutive months, it indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0, or Rank IC is negative over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a broad-based economic contraction that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 and HOUST < 1600.0, or Rank IC for interaction falls below 0.02 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation demand regime (CPIAUCSL > 300.0), rising consumer spending (HOUST and RSAFS) signals strong economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300.0 and HOUST > 1600.0 and RSAFS > 680000.0, or Rank IC for interaction falls below 0.02 over 3-year window.
